did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 9 states that all Israel was registered according to their genealogies, and the records were written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. The same verse explains that Judah was taken into exile in Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.

Did you know? Among the first people to resettle in their towns were not only Israelites, but also priests, Levites, and temple servants—groups with different roles in the life of the nation and in the temple.
Did you know? The people of Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem, along with some descendants of Ephraim and Manasseh. This shows that the city included residents from different families of Israel.

Did you know? The priests living in Jerusalem were listed as heads of their ancestral families, and the text describes them as able men serving in the work of the house of God. Their total number, as given in the verse, was 1,760.
Did you know? The gatekeepers had specific families and duties, including Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman. Shallum is described as the chief gatekeeper.
Did you know? The number of gatekeepers chosen to guard the entrances was 212. The text connects the order of their appointment with David and Samuel the seer and emphasizes their faithfulness.
Did you know? The gatekeepers did more than guard the entrances: they lodged around the house of God, were entrusted with the keys, and were required to open the place every morning.

Did you know? Some of the Levites were entrusted with the utensils used in the service and with the sacred vessels. They had to bring them in and take them out by count—that is, manage them in an orderly and controlled way.

Did you know? The Kohathites were responsible for the bread of the Presence and prepared it every Sabbath. In addition, the priests prepared the spices for the incense, and Mattithiah son of Shallum the Korahite was entrusted with making the griddle cakes.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, Saul’s genealogy is given: Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
